## Definitions

- [statement] Binary Brier loss is the average squared difference between the observed binary outcome and forecast probability. (low confidence) — https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html
- [statement] Binary log loss is the negative log likelihood of the observed label under the predicted probability. (low confidence) — https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html

## How it works

- [statement] A strictly proper scoring rule uniquely minimizes expected penalty when the stated forecast distribution equals the data-generating distribution. (low confidence) — https://rss.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/j.1467-9868.2007.00587.x

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] A Bitcoin futures study reports that five of six evaluated algorithms averaged classification accuracy above 50% across 5–60-minute frequencies in its study period. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8296834

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The cited Brier score paper describes the Brier score as a quadratic measure of probabilistic forecast error. (low confidence) — https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/mwre/132/7/1520-0493_2004_132_1891_oucaar_2.0.co_2.xml

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A calibration-metrics study reports a tradeoff between statistical confidence and probability resolution for binning or kernel methods. (low confidence) — https://jmlr.org/papers/v23/22-0658.html

- [statement] Scikit-learn's DummyClassifier ignores input features and serves as a simple baseline against more complex classifiers. (low confidence) — https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.dummy.DummyClassifier.html
